# Rede Mater Dei - AI Agents for Healthcare Revenue Cycle

<span className="tile-icon tile-icon-svg tile-icon--tag" aria-hidden="true" /> **Workload:** Workflow agent

<span className="tile-icon tile-icon-svg tile-icon--book" aria-hidden="true" /> [Blog Post →](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/rede-mater-dei-de-saude-monitoring-ai-agents-in-the-revenue-cycle-with-amazon-bedrock-agentcore/)

## Architecture

![Rede Mater Dei Architecture](/img/image69.png)

Event-driven multi-agent pipeline for healthcare revenue cycle management.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Billing Event] --> B[Event Router]
    B --> C[Specialized Agent]
    C --> D[AgentCore Runtime]
    D --> E[Bedrock Models]
    E --> F[Claim Data + Docs]
    F --> G[Update Status]
    G --> H[Observability]
```

## Customer Story

**Customer:** Rede Mater Dei de Saúde, a major Brazilian hospital network with 45+ years of service and 8+ locations

**Challenge:** Claim denials jumped to approximately 16% sector-wide, representing about R$10B in lost revenue. Manual, fragmented billing processes were unable to keep pace with regulatory complexity and volume, creating bottlenecks in authorization, coding, and claim validation.

**Solution:** 12 specialized AI agents deployed on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, each focused on a distinct revenue cycle function including claim validation, denial analysis, medical coding checks, authorization requests, and contract verification. Each agent is containerized and runs on AgentCore Runtime, triggered by billing events from hospital EHR systems. Built-in observability captures every execution for audit and continuous improvement.

## Key Technical Decisions

- **Multi-agent decomposition by business function** rather than a monolithic agent. Each agent (claim validation, denial analysis, coding checks, authorization) has bounded scope and clear responsibilities.
- **Custom agents deployed as containers** using the bring-your-own-code pattern. This gave the team full control over agent logic and integration with existing hospital systems.
- **Event-driven architecture** where billing events from EHR systems trigger the relevant agent on demand, keeping compute costs proportional to workload.

## Lessons Learned

- **Start with narrow, high-impact tasks** like authorization validation before expanding to complex workflows. Early wins build organizational trust.
- **Observability is not optional in healthcare** where every decision must be traceable for compliance and quality improvement.
- **Multi-agent beats monolith** when each task has distinct data sources, validation rules, and failure modes.
